title: What qualifications must higher education teaching staff hold under the TEQSA Threshold Standards?
description: What HESF Standard 3.2 requires of Australian academic staff: AQF+1 qualifications or equivalence, teaching skills, oversight and the 2026 amendment.
shortAnswer: Standard 3.2.3 of the Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards) 2021 requires Australian higher education staff who teach, supervise or provide academic oversight to hold a relevant qualification at least one level higher than the course they teach, or equivalent academic, professional or practice-based experience. Doctoral supervisors need a doctorate or equivalent research experience. Staff must also have current disciplinary knowledge and contemporary teaching skills. The Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA) regulates compliance.
keyTakeaways: Standard 3.2.3 has three limbs: current disciplinary knowledge informed by scholarship, research or practice; skills in contemporary teaching, learning and assessment; and a qualification at least one AQF level higher (AQF+1) or equivalent experience.

Teachers who do not fully meet 3.2.3, such as experienced practitioners and teachers in training, may teach specialized components only under the guidance and oversight of staff who do (Standard 3.2.4).

A sixth requirement, that staffing policies on recruitment, retention, promotion, and training and development are inclusive and support diversity, was inserted by the 2026 amendment instrument and applies from July 14, 2026.
TEQSA expects a codified policy for determining equivalence, and time-limited development plans, mentoring or team teaching where an individual does not yet meet all criteria.
TEQSA's staffing guidance note, finalized on June 11, 2025, names inconsistent equivalence decisions and inactive scholarship among the identified compliance risks.
regulator: Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency (TEQSA)
appliesTo: Registered higher education providers in Australia, including universities and independent providers
Academic staff with teaching, supervisory or academic oversight responsibilities, including casual and sessional staff
Academic leaders and committees that appoint staff and determine equivalence

sections.heading: Where does Standard 3.2 sit in the Threshold Standards?

blocks.text: Standard 3.2, Staffing, sits in Part A, Domain 3 (Teaching) of the [Higher Education Standards Framework (Threshold Standards) 2021](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2021L00488/2026-07-14/2026-07-14/text/original/pdf), the legislative instrument TEQSA applies to every registered provider. Domain 3 also contains course design (3.1), learning resources (3.3) and student support (3.4).

This page covers the people who teach. Course structure, learning outcomes and course review are covered in [HESF course design requirements](/regulations/teqsa-hesf-course-design-requirements), and the qualification levels that AQF+1 refers to are explained in [AQF levels and learning outcomes](/regulations/aqf-levels-and-learning-outcomes). Trainers in vocational education follow a different regime: see [RTO trainer and assessor credential requirements](/regulations/rto-trainer-and-assessor-credential-requirements).

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects Compilation No. 2 of the Threshold Standards (compilation date July 14, 2026) as at November 2026. TEQSA guidance notes are principles-based and non-binding; the instrument and the TEQSA Act remain the definitive obligations.
Standard 3.2 has six requirements, covering how many staff a course has, how they are qualified, how less qualified teachers are overseen, student access and inclusive staffing policy.

sections.heading: What does the AQF+1 qualification rule require?

blocks.text: Standard 3.2.3(c) requires "a qualification in a relevant discipline at least one level higher than is awarded for the course of study, or equivalent relevant academic or professional or practice-based experience and expertise, except for staff supervising doctoral degrees having a doctoral degree or equivalent research experience."

In practice, using the levels in the [Australian Qualifications Framework](/regulations/aqf-levels-and-learning-outcomes), a person teaching in a bachelor degree (AQF level 7) needs at least a relevant level 8 qualification, such as an honours degree or graduate diploma, and a person teaching in a master's degree (level 9) needs a relevant doctorate, unless equivalence is established. The qualification must be in a relevant discipline: a higher degree in an unrelated field does not satisfy the rule.

Qualification alone is not enough. Limbs (a) and (b) also require knowledge of contemporary developments in the discipline, "informed by continuing scholarship or research or advances in practice," and skills in contemporary teaching, learning and assessment relevant to the discipline, the role, the mode of delivery and the student cohort. Those two limbs make teaching development and scholarship ongoing obligations rather than one-off hiring checks.

sections.heading: How does TEQSA expect equivalence to be determined?

blocks.text: TEQSA expects equivalence to be decided under a written policy and procedure, not case by case. Its guidance note [Determining equivalence of professional experience and academic qualifications](https://www.teqsa.gov.au/guides-resources/resources/guidance-notes/guidance-note-determining-equivalence-professional-experience-and-academic-qualifications) (version 2.2) says equivalent professional experience "goes well beyond a measure of the time spent by a person working in a particular profession" and must show achievement equivalent to the learning outcomes of the required AQF level in that field.

items: Criteria should be tailored to each field of education and AQF level.
A provider may set a minimum academic qualification, for example at least the AQF level of the course being taught, even where AQF+1 is met through experience.
Evidence can include leadership in professional standards, senior roles requiring expert judgment, awards, advisory board work and peer reviewed publications.
Where an individual does not yet meet all criteria, TEQSA expects an explicit, time-limited professional development plan or strategies such as mentoring or team teaching.
For doctoral supervisors without a doctorate, TEQSA expects analysis of the nature, amount and duration of prior research against the requirements for the relevant research degree.

blocks.text: The equivalence note still cites the 2015 Threshold Standards; the AQF+1 wording it explains carries over into Standard 3.2.3 of the 2021 instrument.

sections.heading: What does TEQSA look for when assessing staffing?

blocks.text: TEQSA looks for workforce planning and governance that produce qualified, current staff in sufficient numbers, not just compliant individual files. Its [staffing guidance note](https://www.teqsa.gov.au/guides-resources/resources/guidance-notes/guidance-note-staffing), finalized on June 11, 2025 after consultation in early 2024, sets out its expectations.

items: A governing body policy framework covering selection and development of staff, including underperforming staff.
Staffing for each course determined by its learning outcomes, the learning needs of students (including access outside formal teaching hours) and the contemporary knowledge the field requires.
For applicants seeking initial registration, a workforce plan showing how staffing will scale with student numbers, with contingency plans for losing key academic staff.
Where a provider relies on casual academic staff, evidence that they keep contemporary skills and knowledge and have enough paid time to teach and support students.

blocks.text: The note lists identified risks, including staff teaching without appropriate qualifications, equivalence decisions that are not "transparent, consistent and appropriate," insufficient oversight under 3.2.4, academic staff not engaged in active scholarship, and insufficient delineation between professional development and scholarly engagement.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records the field of education and AQF level of each unit alongside its learning outcomes, so staffing decisions can be checked against the outcomes a teacher is responsible for. That gives equivalence assessments a concrete reference point and shows where scholarship needs to keep a unit's content current.

faqs.q: Does a sessional tutor need a qualification one level above the course?
faqs.a: Yes, unless equivalence is established or Standard 3.2.4 applies. Standard 3.2.3 covers everyone with teaching and supervisory roles in courses or units, and TEQSA's staffing guidance specifically asks providers relying on casual staff to show those staff keep contemporary skills and have sufficient paid time to teach.

faqs.q: Can industry practitioners teach without AQF+1 qualifications?
faqs.a: Yes, through two routes. A provider can determine that their professional or practice-based experience is equivalent under its equivalence policy, or, if they teach specialized components without fully meeting 3.2.3, their teaching must be guided and overseen by staff who meet the standard under 3.2.4.

The Higher Education Standards Framework Amendment (Threshold Standards) Instrument 2026, registered on July 13, 2026 and commencing the next day, inserted Standard 3.2.6: staffing policies including recruitment, retention, promotion, and training and development must be inclusive and support diversity. Standards 3.2.1 to 3.2.5 were not changed by that instrument.

faqs.q: Is professional development the same as scholarship for Standard 3.2?
faqs.a: No. TEQSA lists insufficient delineation between professional development and scholarly engagement as an identified risk. Standard 3.2.3(a) requires knowledge informed by continuing scholarship, research or advances in practice, so providers should record scholarly activity separately from general staff development.
